claims.explanation: GW-441756 is a selective TrkA (NTRK1) inhibitor, so sensitivity is expected in tumors that depend on NGF/TrkA autocrine or paracrine signaling. The most sensitive lines are enriched for neural-crest-derived lineages (melanoma, neuroblastoma) and for RAS/MAPK pathway activation (BRAF, KRAS, HRAS, NF1, MAP2K1), which can cooperate with TrkA-driven survival/proliferation signaling. Conversely, lines with intact alternative survival pathways or without NTRK1 expression are less affected.

features.basis: GW-441756 is a TrkA/NTRK1 inhibitor; tumors expressing TrkA should be dependent on its signaling
NGF ligand drives TrkA signaling; autocrine NGF supports TrkA-dependent proliferation
BRAF-mutant melanoma lines are among the most sensitive; MAPK activation may cooperate with TrkA
KRAS-mutant lines (neuroblastoma, lung, pancreas) appear enriched among sensitive lines
HRAS-mutant bladder and head/neck lines are among the most sensitive
NF1 loss activates RAS/MAPK and is seen in several sensitive lines
MAP2K1-mutant lung line is highly sensitive, consistent with MAPK dependence
PTEN loss is common in sensitive breast, glioma, and bladder lines
ALK-mutant neuroblastoma and mesothelioma lines are among the least affected
RB1-mutant SCLC and gastric lines are less affected
TP53 mutation is nearly ubiquitous and not discriminating; listed here only as a weak negative correlate
